question: Which cell type contributes most strongly to the spatial transcriptome variance across arterial segments after integration with scRNA-seq data? If cell type annotations are needed, refer to 'author_cell_type'.

nodes.label: Confirm integrated scRNA-seq and Slide-seqV2 object with author_cell_type annotations and aligned feature space
Quantify cell type composition and dominant cell-type signature per spatial spot across arterial segments
Compute transcriptomic variance across arterial segments at the spot level and identify major variance components
Model association between spot-level variance components and cell-type composition/signatures to estimate each cell type’s contribution
Aggregate and compare effect sizes to determine which cell type most strongly explains spatial transcriptome variance across segments
Load integrated AnnData object (scRNA-seq + Slide-seqV2) and verify presence of 'author_cell_type' in scRNA-seq obs and shared gene space
Estimate cell type composition per spatial spot using scRNA-derived author_cell_type signatures and store dominant cell type per spot across arterial segments
Perform spot-level PCA across arterial segments on highly variable genes and extract major variance components
Fit linear models of PCA components as response variables with cell-type composition scores as predictors to estimate each cell type's contribution per component
Aggregate absolute regression coefficients across leading PCs per cell type and identify the cell type with the highest cumulative contribution to spatial transcriptome variance
